events.text: Something is wrong, and you cannot say what. The tea on the White Stairs goes quiet as you pass. A Ministry runner you have known for a century looks down. Two lamps in your hall, which have burned steady since your seat was raised, gutter in the same breath. {hn4_n} people of this isle would see you fall, you realise, and the first name that comes to mind is {npc}'s.

choices.text: Ask quietly who has been visiting whom

effects.log: You ask. The answers are small and awkward, and together they begin to look like a shape.

choices.text: Call it nerves, and drink your tea

effects.log: You drink it. The tea is the last ordinary thing for a while.

events.text: A cloud-barge lingers off your landing at dusk with no banner, no cargo, and a crew that sit very still. By morning it is gone. In the Cloud Library a scroll is a finger-width out of its rack, as if someone had meant to take it and thought better. {npc} meets your eye across the courtyard a moment too long, and then looks away at nothing.

choices.text: Have the landing watched for the barge

effects.log: You post a watcher. The barge does not return, but a second does, and this one has a flag.

choices.text: Reshelve the scroll, and think no more of it

effects.log: You reshelve it. The thought refuses to go quietly, and it is still waiting when you wake.

events.text: One of your own disciples has been missing from morning practice, and was seen at the Ministry Isles in the company of a stranger with fine sleeves. When the disciple returns, there is a new jade token at their belt and a look in their eyes you have seen on others, long ago. {npc} is the one who recommended them to your isle, years back.

choices.text: Follow the disciple on the next errand

choices.text: Say nothing, and let the disciple keep the token

effects.log: You say nothing. The disciple is polite and terrible at hiding it. The token remains on the belt.

events.text: A rumour is going round the isles that your breakthrough was bought, not earned: a debt to a Demon Realm duke, a stolen pill, a theft from the Nine Clouds. It is told as gossip. It is told at too many tables to be gossip. When you trace it, it runs through three mouths to one: {npc}, at a feast, in an unguarded moment, over a very small cup.

choices.text: Follow the rumour to its first teller

effects.log: You find the first teller, who is more frightened than proud. The words were written for them. You keep the script.

choices.text: Let the gossip find its own level

effects.log: The gossip finds its level, which is higher than you hoped.

events.text: Your spirit-stone shipments from the lower isles come late, then half, then not at all. The cloud-barge captains who used to love your custom are suddenly full of excuses. A rival faction has bought their contracts, you are told, for a handsome sum. Behind the rival you glimpse {npc}'s hand on the ledger, light as a bird, and quite sure of itself.

choices.text: Send a quiet agent to buy the contracts back

effects.log: The agent returns with a thinner purse and the name of the buyer. It is the name you expected.

choices.text: Live on your stores, and wait out the squeeze

effects.log: The stores hold, for a while. The squeeze, you notice, has not been designed to end.

choices.text: Buy them off, in the quiet way of the isles

events.text: It is a dinner, of course. The great hall of the Ministry Isles is set for eleven, with the finest cups, and when you enter every seat but one is taken. {npc} rises as if to greet you. Behind {him}, a dozen of the faction's guard stand against the wall in the quiet way of people who have been told to wait. The soup is excellent. It is still steaming.

choices.text: Overturn the table, and fight your way out

fail.log: You overturn the table. It is not enough. You leave through a window you remember from your youth, bleeding a little, and not in good order.

choices.text: Bow to the host, decline the soup, and leave the isles

events.text: One of your own lesser gods has been missing from the dawn rite, and was seen at the border shrines in the company of a stranger in fine vestments. When they return they wear a new charm at the belt and a look in their eyes you have seen on others long ago. {npc} is the one who recommended them to your temple, years back.

choices.text: Follow the lesser god on the next errand

choices.text: Say nothing, and let them keep the charm

effects.log: You say nothing. They are polite and terrible at hiding it. The charm remains.

events.text: A rumour is going about the pantheons that your ascension was bought, not earned: a debt to an Elder Lineage, a stolen name, a theft from another pantheon's altar. It is told as gossip. It is told at too many tables to be gossip. When you trace it, it runs through three mouths to one: {npc}, at a feast, in an unguarded moment, over a small cup.

choices.text: Follow the rumour to its first teller

effects.log: You find the first teller, who is more frightened than proud. The words were written for them. You keep the script.

choices.text: Let the gossip find its own level

effects.log: The gossip finds its level, which is higher than you hoped.

events.text: The offerings from your outer villages come late, then half, then not at all. The pilgrims who used to love your shrines are suddenly full of excuses. A rival pantheon has bought their favour, you are told, with a handsome gift of rain. Behind the rival you glimpse {npc}'s hand in the ledger of offerings, light as a bird, and quite sure of itself.

choices.text: Send a quiet priest to win the villages back

effects.log: The priest returns with a thinner pouch and the name of the buyer. It is the name you expected.

choices.text: Live on your stores, and wait out the squeeze

effects.log: The stores hold, for a while. The squeeze, you notice, has not been designed to end.

events.text: You know now. It is no longer a feeling. {npc} stands behind {hn4_n} others, and the plan runs through the Book of Fates, a rival pantheon's seal, and a debt owed to an Elder Lineage you thought neutral. You have the letters. You have, you find, rather more evidence than you wanted. A decision is waiting for you in the lamplight.

choices.text: Strike first, with everything you have

effects.log: You gather your proof and your power and strike. It is quick, ugly, and entirely without ritual.

choices.text: Buy them off, in the quiet way of the pantheons

effects.log: You send a very polite invitation and a very large gift. The plot loosens like a knot in warm water.

choices.text: Walk into it on purpose, and see who is waiting

effects.log: You accept an invitation you know to be a trap. You go with your vestments pressed and your temper cool.

events.text: The last piece falls into place on a quiet evening at the shrine of the sick. A dying priestess, in no great hurry, tells you who paid for the curse that was never cast, and why. It is {npc}, and a handful of others whose names are on the list. It is said plainly, the way one sets down a heavy basket, with a request for nothing but a cup of water.

choices.text: Strike first; the list is enough

effects.log: You take the list and move before the night is out. By morning half the names are on the road.

choices.text: Send each name a gift, and a question

effects.log: The gifts go out. The answers come back in a week, and they are, on the whole, relieved.

choices.text: Let the plot play out, and be there at the end

effects.log: You tell no one. You sit in your hall with the lamps lit and the door ajar.

events.text: The trap closes at the turn of the season: a summons to the Heavenly Court, a corridor of white stone, and {npc} at the far end with {hn4_n} others and the Book open. The doors shut behind you with a sound like a long breath. They do not speak. They have prepared for you the way a mason prepares a keystone, and they are very good.

choices.text: Break the circle, and take {npc} as you pass

ok.log: The corridor is white and then it is not. When it ends, the Book is shut, the doors are open, and {npc} is no longer standing.

fail.log: The circle holds. You are driven against the doors, cracked at the ribs, with a Transgression in your enemy's hand.

choices.text: Turn back, and leave the domain by the lower road

effects.log: You turn. The lower road is long and cold and empty, and the plot lets you walk it.

events.text: It is a feast, of course. The great hall of the rival pantheon is set for eleven, with the finest cups, and when you enter every seat but one is taken. {npc} rises as if to greet you. Behind {him}, a dozen shrine-guards stand against the wall in the quiet way of those told to wait. The soup is excellent. It is still steaming.

choices.text: Overturn the table, and fight your way out

ok.log: The table is old and heavy and goes over beautifully. The rest is quick work, and in the end the soup is the only casualty.

fail.log: You overturn the table. It is not enough. You leave through a window you remember from your youth, bleeding a little, and not in good order.

choices.text: Bow to the host, decline the soup, and leave the domain

effects.log: You decline with perfect courtesy. Nobody stops you, and everybody watches you go.

events.text: Ten years on, the lower road is the same. A new lamp-seller has the old one's stall, and does not know your face. The temples are smaller than you remembered, and brighter. Your altar is open, and its doors stand ajar. The old cook is there, older, and sets a bowl on the step as if you had gone out for water. You cannot speak. You eat.

effects.log: It receives you exactly as it did. Nobody asks how you came back, and nobody needs to.

choices.text: Walk the cloister first, and touch every stone

events.text: You come back at dusk, on a borrowed cloud, with the same staff. The Court has quietly let the Transgression lapse, and the Book has your name again, in smaller ink. Messengers of the pantheons bow to you on the steps, carefully. Nobody mentions the ten years. You are home, and home has learned a new way to be polite.

choices.text: Greet them all by name, one at a time

effects.log: It takes an hour. At the end of it you are more at home than when you began.

choices.text: Go straight to your hall, and shut the door

effects.log: You shut it. The silence in your own hall is the best you have heard in a decade.

events.text: Something is wrong, and you cannot say what. Travellers on the road speak low as you pass. A courier of the king's, whom you have known for years, looks down. choices.text: Ask quietly who has been visiting whom

effects.log: You ask. The answers are small and awkward, and together they begin to look like a shape.

choices.text: Call it nerves, and finish your supper

events.text: Ten years on, the lower road is the same. A new baker has the old one's oven, and does not know your face. The valley is smaller than you remembered, and brighter. Your hall is open, its doors ajar. The old cook is there, older, and sets a bowl on the table as if you had gone out for water. You cannot speak. You eat.

choices.text: Sit in your old chair, and say nothing

effects.log: It fits you exactly as it did. Nobody asks how you came back, and nobody needs to.

choices.text: Walk the yard first, and touch every stone

effects.log: The stones are warm. There is a new crack in one, and you put your thumb in it.

events.text: You come back at dusk, on a borrowed horse, with the same sword. The king has quietly let the warrant lapse, and the rolls have your name again, in smaller ink. Magistrates bow to you in the street, carefully. Nobody mentions the ten years. You are home, and home has learned a new way to be polite.

choices.text: Greet them all by name, one at a time

effects.log: It takes an hour. At the end of it you are more at home than when you began.

choices.text: Go straight to your hall, and shut the door

effects.log: You shut it. The silence in your own hall is the best you have heard in a decade.
